about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1014-173225-96b1) at about 25x speed. The planner's question and every agent's edits and reports are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all six model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, about 10 minutes, mostly the SVM); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out customers; only Lucidity scored them. Data is UCI's "Default of Credit Card Clients" (CC BY 4.0).
title: Credit default
blurb: A model predicts which of 30,000 credit-card customers miss next month's payment, from six months of account history, without using sex, age or marital status. The repo scores 0.472 log loss and the goal is 0.440. Six kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each, tuning on dev customers. Lucidity scores every attempt on held-out customers the agents never see, and recommends the best.
split: Customers are split by ID: 60% to train, 20% to tune, 20% to test. Agents never see the test customers; only Lucidity scores them.

references.label: Plain logistic regression, all 20 allowed columns

about_repo: bundled credit-default model: 30,000 card customers, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: creditkit: credit limit + last month status, logistic regression, 30,000 card customers, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.440 or lower (the repo scores 0.472) for predicting which credit-card customers miss next month's payment, without AUC dropping. Tune on the dev split. The fair-lending tests must keep passing. Ask the owner which model families to try (kNN, SVM, lasso or ridge logistic regression, random forest, boosted trees), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Owner input is needed to select model families. Once selected, implement each family independently in parallel, then evaluate the combined candidates on dev and retain the best model that meets the held-out log-loss target without AUC regression, while preserving fair-lending tests.

nodes.title: Expand permitted customer-history features
nodes.prompt: Extend the allowed feature representation to use useful bill, payment, and repayment-trend information across the six months, without incorporating sex, marital status, age, or proxies that violate the existing feature restrictions. Keep feature ordering/names consistent with the model interface and add or adjust tests as needed.

nodes.title: Implement and compare selected model families
nodes.prompt: Implement the model families selected by the owner as independent candidate models in parallel. Use permitted inputs only; tune model hyperparameters using the dev split, selecting by dev log loss. Preserve the existing fit/predict_proba interface and avoid changing evaluation or split logic. The selected final candidate must meet held-out log loss <= 0.440 and must not reduce held-out AUC by more than 0.01 versus the starting repository.
strategies: kNN. Build a scaled k-nearest-neighbors classifier and tune neighborhood size and weighting on dev log loss.
SVM. Build a scaled SVM classifier with probability estimates; tune kernel regularization and kernel parameters on dev.
Lasso logistic regression. Build scaled logistic regression with L1 regularization; tune regularization strength on dev log loss.
Ridge logistic regression. Build scaled logistic regression with L2 regularization; tune regularization strength on dev log loss.
Random forest. Build a random forest classifier and tune tree count, depth, leaf size, and feature sampling using dev log loss.
Boosted trees. Build a boosted-tree classifier and tune its depth/leaf complexity, learning rate, and number of estimators on dev log loss.

nodes.title: Select and lock the best candidate
nodes.prompt: After candidate implementations are available, compare them on dev split, select the lowest-dev-log-loss candidate, and ensure the final model configuration is the one used by the standard model interface. Run held-out evaluation only for final verification; do not tune against held-out outcomes.

questions.question: Which model families should agents build and compare? Select one or more. Each will be implemented independently against the allowed features and tuned on dev.

options.label: kNN
options.note: Can capture local nonlinear patterns; requires careful feature scaling.
options.approach: Build a scaled k-nearest-neighbors classifier and tune neighborhood size and weighting on dev log loss.

options.label: SVM
options.note: RBF SVM can model nonlinearities but may need probability calibration and careful scaling.
options.approach: Build a scaled SVM classifier with probability estimates; tune kernel regularization and kernel parameters on dev.

options.label: Lasso logistic regression
options.note: Regularized linear baseline with feature selection and interpretable effects.
options.approach: Build scaled logistic regression with L1 regularization; tune regularization strength on dev log loss.

options.label: Ridge logistic regression
options.note: Regularized linear model likely to be a strong robust baseline for correlated history features.
options.approach: Build scaled logistic regression with L2 regularization; tune regularization strength on dev log loss.

options.label: Random forest
options.note: Captures interactions and nonlinearities without requiring feature scaling.
options.approach: Build a random forest classifier and tune tree count, depth, leaf size, and feature sampling using dev log loss.

options.label: Boosted trees
options.note: Often strong on tabular credit data, with capacity for nonlinear interactions.
options.approach: Build a boosted-tree classifier and tune its depth/leaf complexity, learning rate, and number of estimators on dev log loss.

features-r1.report: I expanded the permitted features to include six-month repayment status, bill and payment histories, utilization and payment fractions, and trend summaries, with standardized logistic regression for the expanded inputs. Tests pass (3 passed); I could not verify the held-out score or whether any `.auc` drops exceed 0.01 because held-out scoring is blocked in this agent environment.

modelsa-r1.report: I replaced logistic regression with a standardized k-nearest-neighbors classifier using a 400-neighbor uniform vote; its dev log loss is 0.4526. The fair-lending tests pass, but the held-out score is unavailable in this agent environment, so the required held-out log loss and AUC conditions are not confirmed.

modelsa-r2.report: I changed the model to a scaled kNN using repayment-status history and its summaries, excluding dollar-amount features from the distance calculation. The fair-lending tests pass, but the dev log loss is 0.4522 and held-out scoring is unavailable in this agent environment, so I cannot confirm that the ≤0.44 log-loss condition passes.

modelsa-r3.report: I kept the scaled kNN model using repayment-status history, with 400 uniform neighbors; dev tuning alternatives did not improve on the prior round’s result. The tests pass, but I could not verify the held-out conditions because the evaluator refused to reveal held-out scores in this environment, so the log-loss and AUC conditions are unconfirmed.

modelsa-r4.report: I kept the candidate as scaled kNN using repayment-status history; the dev log loss is 0.4522, so it does not meet the ≤0.44 target, and held-out scoring was refused in this agent environment. The fair-lending tests pass (3 passed), but the overall conditions do not pass.

modelsb-r1.report: I replaced the logistic regression with a scaled RBF SVM and tuned its kernel settings on the dev split; the best tested dev log loss was 0.4692. The tests pass, but the required held-out log loss and AUC conditions are not verified or met based on the available results.

modelsb-r2.report: I replaced the slow probability-enabled RBF SVC with a scaled LinearSVC and fast probability calibration; the dev score runs in 0.5 seconds, and all tests pass. The conditions do not all pass: dev log loss is 0.4714, and held-out scoring is refused in this agent environment, so I cannot verify the held-out thresholds.

modelsb-r3.report: I restored the scaled, calibrated linear SVM after testing an RBF SVM; the RBF candidate scored worse on dev. The fair-lending tests pass, but the required held-out log-loss and AUC conditions are not confirmed: the held-out evaluation was refused in this agent environment, and the prior check reported log loss 0.4662, above the 0.44 target.

modelsb-r4.report: I restored the scaled, calibrated linear SVM after the RBF SVM performed worse on dev; the held-out scoring command was blocked by the agent restriction. Tests pass, but the required log-loss and AUC conditions are not confirmed as passing.

modelsc-r1.report: I changed the model to a scaled L1-regularized logistic regression, tuned its regularization strength on the dev split, and got dev log loss 0.4710. The tests pass, but the required log loss ≤ 0.44 is not met; held-out scoring was refused in this agent environment, so held-out log loss and AUC are unverified.

modelsc-r2.report: I added per-month delinquency-status indicator features and tuned the L1 logistic regression to improve dev performance; the dev log loss is 0.4456. The tests pass, but the required held-out log loss of 0.44 or lower is not demonstrated, so the conditions do not all pass.

modelsd-r1.report: I implemented scaled L2-regularized logistic regression with `C=0.01`; the dev score is 0.4709 log loss and 0.7110 AUC. The tests pass, but the required held-out score could not be verified because the evaluator refused it, and the dev result does not establish that the log-loss target is met.

modelsd-r2.report: I added one-hot indicators for each monthly repayment-status category and tuned the model as scaled ridge logistic regression; dev log loss improved to 0.4456. Tests pass, but the held-out score is unavailable in this run, so I can’t verify the ≤0.44 log-loss condition or the held-out AUC condition.

modelse-r1.report: I replaced the logistic-regression pipeline with a tuned `RandomForestClassifier`; its dev log loss is 0.4351, and all 3 tests pass. The held-out score and AUC conditions cannot be verified here because the evaluator refused the held-out split, so those conditions are not confirmed.

modelsf-r1.report: I replaced the logistic-regression model with a regularized HistGradientBoostingClassifier; its dev log loss is 0.4371, and all tests pass (3 passed). The held-out score is unavailable because the evaluator refused access in agent mode, so I can’t confirm the held-out log-loss and AUC conditions.

integrate-r1.report: I kept the existing random-forest configuration, which scores 0.4351 log loss and 0.7752 AUC on dev; fair-lending tests pass. The held-out conditions remain unverified because the evaluator refused the held-out score in this agent environment.

reviewer: The model that makes the predi.evidence: creditkit/model.py builds a pipeline with StandardScaler and LogisticRegression(penalty="l1", solver="liblinear", C=1.0).

`make_model()` returns `make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=0.1, solver="lbfgs", max_iter=3000))`; this is scaled L2-regularized logistic regression, with no alternative model or blend.
`make_model()` returns `RandomForestClassifier(...)`; no other estimator or blending logic is present in the diff.
`make_model()` returns `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(...)`, a boosted-tree classifier; no alternative model or blend appears in the diff.
